subject: MAP: performance gating and close timeline for CloudBank pilot
message_1_subject: MAP: performance gating and close timeline for CloudBank pilot
message_1_body:
Carlos —

Thanks for the sync today. Per our discussion, I pulled together a concise MAP annex that scopes the performance evaluation we need before CloudBank signs the production contract. Attached is a starter workbook (MAP_v1_scope.xlsx) but I summarized the key scoping decisions below so we can lock the runway by Friday.

Scope (proposed):
- Workload profiles: interactive search (short prompts, avg tokens output ~40), report generation (long-form, avg 450 tokens), and embedding batch jobs (1k items per minute).
- Traffic shape: baseline steady-state 20 QPS for interactive, 5 concurrent long-form writers, and burst test to 80 QPS for 2 minutes to validate autoscaling/backpressure.
- Models: r-infer-7b-quant (primary) + r-infer-13b-fallback for latency-sensitive requests.
- Metrics to collect: TTFT (time-to-first-token), p50/p95/p99 latency for first-token and tail, tokens/sec throughput, cold-start time, KV-cache hit rate, and error rate (500s/429s).

Success criteria (pass/fail gating):
1) Interactive p95 TTFT <= 300ms at 20 QPS.
2) Long-form throughput >= 6 tokens/sec per GPU with p95 tail latency <= 1.2s at 5 concurrent writers.
3) System sustains burst to 80 QPS for 2 minutes with <1% error rate and automatic fallback to 13b when latency exceeds 1s.

Timeline items:
- Wed (5/27): Redwood runs the canonical bench against CloudBank sample dataset + synthetic burst window.
- Thu (5/28): Deliver CSV of raw metrics and short runbook describing any deviations + recommended config changes.
- Mon (6/1): If pass, CloudBank signs SOW and we schedule Dedicated capacity. If fail, we follow defined remediation steps in the MAP annex.

Ask: Please confirm the workload profiles above (especially token averages) and confirm access to the 10k sample prompts we discussed. If you want any adjust to gating numbers we can iterate today — goal is to avoid a second round of runs.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: MAP_v1_scope.xlsx (workbook with test harness details and sample prompt list)

message_3_subject: Re: MAP: performance gating and close timeline for CloudBank pilot — bench plan notes
message_3_body:
Team —

I updated the workbook with concrete harness configs (attached) and a short checklist for the Wed run. Key changes:
- Added a 60-token interactive sensitivity run (3 minute sustained at 20 QPS).
- Set measurement windows: warm-up 90s, steady-state 10m, tail sampling every 30s for p99 estimates.
- Added a KV-cache exercise: prefix-heavy workload to validate cache hit/miss behavior (target >80% hit for interactive).

Remediation steps if gating fails:
A) If interactive p95 TTFT in 20 QPS steady-state >300ms: enable continuous batching with batch_timeout 5ms and re-run.
B) If token throughput for long-form <6 tokens/sec per GPU: switch to 13b-fallback for long jobs and benchmark model-split routing.
C) If burst >80 QPS causes >1% error: apply request-queuing with 100ms circuit-breaker and re-run.

I'll be on the call Wed to watch traces and surface any infra flags.

Marissa
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: MAP_v1_scope.xlsx (updated with harness configs)
message_4_subject: MAP: benchmark results + recommended configs (final) — CloudBank pilot
message_4_body:
Carlos / Liz —

We completed the MAP runs Wed morning and attached the raw CSV and a short summary PDF. High-level results and recommended next steps below.

Summary (pass/fail against gating):
- Interactive (20 QPS, median output ~40 tokens): p50 TTFT = 110ms; p95 TTFT = 260ms (PASS: <=300ms).
- Sensitivity run (60-token median): p95 TTFT = 410ms (DEGRADATION noted — still within acceptable for one path, not primary).
- Long-form (5 concurrent writers): sustained throughput 7.1 tokens/sec per GPU, p95 tail = 1.05s (PASS).
- Burst test (80 QPS, 2 min): error rate = 0.6% and automatic model routing to 13b engaged for ~18% of requests where TTL exceeded 1s (PASS).

Operational observations:
- KV-cache hit rate for interactive profile averaged 84% after warm-up — aligns with expected hit patterns for prefix-heavy queries.
- Cold-starts: cold-container median start time 1.8s — we recommend a warm pool for low-latency lanes.
- TTFT improvements achieved by continuous batching (5ms timeout) + small increase in prefetched KV cache size.

Recommended MAP annex updates (attached in MAP-final-cloudbank.pdf):
1) Include 60-token interactive path as a non-blocking metric (informational) — primary gating remains 40-token profile.
2) Add warm-pool requirement for production lanes to keep cold-starts <1.0s for <5% of requests.
3) Define rollback window: 48 hours post-deploy to monitor quality metrics (we'll provide eval snapshots).

Next steps / close timeline:
- Thu (5/29): We deliver final MAP annex PDF + SOW draft (attached).
- Mon (6/1): Target signature if MAP annex accepted.
- Tue (6/2): Provision Dedicated capacity and kickoff Ops handoff.

Attachments:
- benchmark-results-20260527.csv (raw metrics from runs)
- MAP-final-cloudbank.pdf (annex with runbook & SLOs)

If you'd like, we can also schedule an optional 30-minute readout early next week to walk the CloudBank engineering team through the traces and routing behavior.

Thanks for the quick coordination — pleased we could validate the SLOs in one pass.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
